Debugger notification contract and virtual breakpoint synthesis details.
Virtual-mode trap redirection and bus-lock handling internals.
Trap signal construction and signal code selection for debug, floating-point and virtualization faults.
Fixup, die and notification helpers for kernel traps and dynamic shared object exception handling.
Floating-point state synchronization and exception classification helpers.
Extended-feature enabling helper and error register layout.
Trust-domain virtualization info retrieval and handling plus guest info layout.
General-protection-like fault helpers and trap address helpers.

findings.text: Debug exception has separate kernel-only, user-only, flexible raw and flexible event-data entry forms that all classify privilege and forward a captured debug status word to a kernel or user handler.

User debug handling preserves stepping indication in per-thread virtual status, aligns block-step tracking with hardware clearing, gives debugger notification first chance at the trap, and afterwards considers virtual mode redirection, bus handling and trap-signal delivery before returning to user.
Empty hardware debug status is treated as a single-byte trap cause requesting a trap signal, while non-empty status merges architected trap bits with virtual thread bits for signal decisions.

User debug path deliberately leaves global debug control uncleared across code that may schedule or fault, accepting a possible nested debug trap that is expected to be resolved on the kernel path where stack protection differs.

User debug path brackets debugger consultation with entry-from-user and instrumentation markers and only permits interrupts after debug status is safely recorded, disabling them again before exit to user.
Processor and vector floating-point errors share one handler selected by trap number, with dedicated entry points for coprocessor error and vector error.

Kernel-origin floating faults prefer fixup and layered notification before termination, while user-origin faults synchronize floating state, classify the cause, and deliver a floating-point fault to the offending task.
Unclassifiable floating-point causes are treated as spurious and suppressed without signaling, and dynamic shared object fixups are attempted before any signal.
Spurious interrupt bug entry is intentionally empty to absorb a reserved vector that some local interrupt configurations may emit for removed interrupts.

Extended feature events are detected by reading a dedicated error register, cleared immediately, rejected in kernel context, and otherwise resolved by enabling the requested feature with permission and fault failures mapped to distinct fatal signals.
Device-not-available entry first attempts extended-feature resolution and only then examines task-switched state.
Unexpected device-not-available with task-switched flag set warns and clears the flag to continue, while other unexpected cases terminate the context rather than risk a repeated fault loop.
Virtualization fault delivery signals segmentation to user contexts and attempts fixup plus notification before address-specific termination in kernel contexts.

Virtualization exception entry always captures virtualization info first with asynchronous events held off, enables interrupts conditionally, delegates to a virtualization handler, and falls back to fault raising on failure.
Virtualization info capture is protected from nesting by keeping non-maskable, machine-check and regular interrupts disabled until the info fetch completes.
Return-instruction error entry enables interrupts around debugger notification and falls back to an illegal-instruction trap with bad-stack indication when notification does not stop processing.

Early trap setup orders entry-area creation before stack use, guest handling and task-state setup before trap installation, and processor initialization last, skipping legacy trap table setup when an alternate return mechanism is present.

Early trap initialization, scheduler clock readers, calibration routines, suspend and resume state helpers and recalibration are provided as cross-file interfaces alongside globally visible processor and timestamp frequency variables and a clocksource reliability flag.
Cycle-to-nanosecond conversion state holds two generation data slots plus a latch sequence counter and is sized to fit one cache line for lock-free readers.
Always-running-timer base clock object carries a dedicated always-running-timer clocksource identifier and a presence flag tracks availability.

Conversion-scale updates are serialized against interrupts with idle notifications around the change, readers disable preemption without tracing, and suspend-resume preserves monotonicity by rebasing offsets under interrupt protection across both slots and every possible processor.
Scheduler clock prefers timestamp-counter conversion when a static key indicates availability and otherwise derives nanoseconds from tick counts relative to boot baseline.
Scheduler clock intentionally continues using a timestamp counter marked unstable for timekeeping because small scheduling errors are preferable to loss of speed.
Frequency scaling factor KHZ has value one thousand.
Calibration allows five retries and the default timestamp threshold value is 0x20000.
Short calibration window is ten milliseconds with one thousand loop iterations and long window is fifty milliseconds with five thousand iterations, with latch values derived from interval timer rate.
Fast interval timer calibration is bounded to fifty milliseconds with iteration bound derived from timer rate and a two-hundred-fifty-six count quantum.
Minimum denominator for always-running-timer ratio is one.
Virtualization fault label is a short two-word text constant used for user signals and kernel diagnostics.
Timestamp watchdog configuration supports automatic, disabled and enabled modes selected by boot option.

Early processor frequency discovery prefers processor identification, then model-specific registers, then fast interval-timer probing, while full discovery falls back to combined timer methods and non-symmetric recalibration reconciles processor and timestamp rates within a ten percent tolerance.

Timestamp calibration by processor identification applies only to one vendor with minimum leaf levels, synthesizes missing crystal rates from base frequency and ratio, hardcodes a twenty-five megahertz crystal for one system-on-chip family and marks timestamp as known frequency and reliable where appropriate.

Register-based frequency discovery selects ratio and bus reference by matched processor table, computes timestamp and bus rates with rounding, programs local timer period when available, and forces known-frequency and reliable markings.
Fast interval-timer probing runs with interrupts saved and restored to avoid timing disturbance.
Suspend captures scheduler clock only when timestamp use or stable clock warrants it, and resume rebases all per-processor conversion offsets by the suspend-to-resume delta.

Frequency-change handling marks timestamp unstable on multiprocessor systems, captures reference frequency on first change, rescales loop timing and timestamp rate on directional transitions, updates conversion scale, and registers only when timestamp exists without invariant behavior.
Timestamp clocksource provides ordered counter reads, marks itself used on enable, verifies adjustment on resume, and coordinates stable-tick and unstable transitions with scheduler clock stability.

Fast interval-timer calibration requires legacy interrupt hardware, validates high-byte stability over many samples, demands sub-five-hundred-parts-per-million error with early abort on hopeless error, and fails to zero on any instability.
Timestamp boot option recognizes reliability, interrupt-time exclusion, forced instability, watchdog control and forced recalibration keywords, plus a separate early frequency override.
Frequency changes on more than one online processor unconditionally mark timestamp unstable without rescaling.
Successful crystal or bus frequency discovery also seeds local timer period to avoid later calibration when local interrupt support is compiled in.
